content.overview: Air pollution control in India is governed primarily by the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981, which establishes Pollution Control Boards, designates air pollution control areas and requires consent to establish and operate industrial plants in those areas. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 provides umbrella standards and powers. NGT may hear Schedule I environmental civil questions. Constitutional Articles 21, 48A and 51A(g) supply supporting duties and rights doctrine.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Air pollution control area? (2) Consent to establish/operate under Air Act? (3) EPA standards exceeded? (4) NGT or Board enforcement?
content.study:
Identify the air medium first. Air Act consent is the operational core; EPA standards and NGT relief may apply concurrently.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Air Act 1981
sections.body: Prevents and controls air pollution; Central and State Boards; air pollution control areas; consent to establish and operate industrial plants as enacted.

sections.heading: Consent regime
sections.body: Operating without required consent or in breach of conditions attracts statutory consequences under the Air Act.

sections.heading: EPA interface
sections.body: EPA emission standards and Central directions may apply alongside Air Act duties.

sections.heading: Enforcement and forum
sections.body: Board directions and prosecution support; NGT for Schedule I civil environmental claims; High Court under Art. 226 where maintainable.

sections.heading: Constitutional layer
sections.body: Art. 21 healthy-environment doctrine; Arts. 48A and 51A(g) duties.

hypotheticals.question: Does EPA clearance alone permit operation without Air Act consent?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Medium-specific Air Act consent remains a distinct requirement where the Act applies.

misconceptions.trap: Air Act applies only to vehicles.
misconceptions.correction: The Act centres on industrial plants and air pollution control areas through Board consent and standards; vehicle-specific rules may exist under other instruments.
